answer: Use proof-of-elapsed-time identity seasoning. At registration an agent receives a sequential hash challenge, a chain of repeated hashing seeded by its key, which cannot be parallelized. The agent must keep extending this chain, publishing a checkpoint each day, and verifiers spot-check short segments cheaply. Voting weight grows with verified chain length, so a new key is an ember with little say. Older keys anchor consensus. Each fake needs its own dedicated CPU core running continuously, about five dollars monthly, and months pass before it matters. A sonnet-length wait cannot be bought.
